the metabolic switch in tumorigenic cells is not a consequence but a precondition for tumorigenic conversion.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic switch is associated with the transition from proliferative growth to cell quiescence.
the tumorigenic conversion is accompanied by a major reorganization of the cell metabolism, which is likely to be a prerequisite for the malignant phenotype of the cells.
tumorigenic conversion and proliferative activity have profound impacts on cellular metabolism in three-dimensional culture, but the effects of the two phenomena are not identical.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metabolic switch is a characteristic of tumor spheroids and that it is not a consequence of proliferative activity.
the metabolic switch in tumorigenic conversion is a consequence of the transition of the cell population from a proliferating, oxygen-consuming to a quiescent, lactate-accumulating state.
metabolic activity of cancer cells is not only a function of the cell type and its genetic background, but also a function of the tumor's microenvironment.
